name: Sandy Li
current_role: Likely co-founder, Trendy International Group (Guangzhou fashion group behind Ochirly) - unconfirmed
profile: Listed by Hurun (2014-2016) as sharing a fortune with Jack Xu from Trendy, the Guangzhou apparel group founded in 1999 (Ochirly, Five Plus, Trendiano). Sources name Xu's wife and co-founder as Li Shanhu (Shanhu Li); whether 'Sandy Li' is the same person could not be confirmed.
interesting_fact: Trendy International was the first Chinese apparel group to receive investment from LVMH's L Capital Asia (about $200m, 2012-13) and grew to roughly 3,000 stores in 290 Chinese cities.
notes: Identity ambiguous: the English name 'Sandy Li' does not appear in sources; likely refers to Li Shanhu (李珊瑚), co-founder with husband Jacky Xu (Xu Yu). Very low public profile; route would be via Trendy Group corporate channels.

name: Sandeep Engineer
current_role: Founder and Managing Director, Astral Ltd (Ahmedabad, India)
profile: Chemical engineer (L D College, 1981) who began in pharma at Cadila before running his own bulk-drug ventures. After studying polymers in the US in 1997, he launched Astral in 1999 as India's first CPVC pipe maker, convincing plumbers to switch from metal; Astral now also makes adhesives, sealants and other building products.
interesting_fact: Astral was India's only CPVC pipe manufacturer when it started production in 1999, and had a hard time convincing customers that plastic pipes could outperform metal ones; it later used film stars as brand ambassadors.
deep_cut_fact: His first venture (1982) was Shree Trading, a pharma-formulation trading business run from a rented spot on Biscuit Gali off Ahmedabad's Relief Road with Rs 40,000, marketing GDCL's Isabgol products. He had joined Cadila in 1981 on Rs 850 a month. His motto: 'If we think we can, we will.'
notes: Contact is Astral's general corporate email (also listed on the investors page). He has given interviews to The CEO Magazine (theceomagazine.com) and is reasonably accessible to business media.

name: George Hearst, Jr.
current_role: Deceased (was Chairman of the Board, Hearst Corporation, 1996-2012)
profile: George Randolph Hearst Jr., eldest grandson of William Randolph Hearst, chaired Hearst Corporation from 1996 until his death on June 25, 2012, aged 84, at Stanford University Medical Center after complications from a stroke.
notes: Died June 25, 2012 (Hearst Corporation press release, globenewswire, June 26, 2012). Not a candidate for outreach.

name: Alfons Doblinger
current_role: Founder, controlling shareholder and managing director, Doblinger Unternehmensgruppe (incl. DIBAG Industriebau AG), Munich; major shareholder of Bauer AG
profile: Bavarian builder-turned-landlord who founded the Munich-based Doblinger group (design, construction and management of property) and remains one of Munich's largest property owners, with roughly 19,600 apartments and a large commercial portfolio. Still running the group in his 80s; he is also the largest shareholder of foundation-engineering firm Bauer AG.
interesting_fact: He first came to public attention in 1990 when he bought the Bavarian portfolio of the trade-union housing company Neue Heimat - more than 32,500 apartments - for just under 1 billion D-Mark.
deep_cut_fact: Born and raised in the Bavarian Forest (an 'Oberpfälzer'), he started his business at 23 in 1967 according to Börsen-Zeitung (Forbes dates it to 1962 at 17), and was still the group's Geschäftsführer at 78.
notes: Described by Börsen-Zeitung as 'der scheue' (the shy one): avoids publicity and declined to answer the paper's questions. Expect low responsiveness; corporate email via DIBAG is the only published route.

name: David Chow
current_role: Macau businessman; co-founder and former co-chairman of Macau Legend Development (developer of Macau Fisherman's Wharf); no longer on its board
profile: Hong Kong-born (1950) Macau entrepreneur and former legislator (13 years, until 2009) who developed Macau Fisherman's Wharf, the themed waterfront complex opened 2005-06, and co-founded Macau Legend Development in 2006, which ran the Babylon and Pharaoh's Palace casinos under SJM's licence. He has since exited the board and cut his stake to a fraction of a percent.
interesting_fact: Fisherman's Wharf was built partly on reclaimed land (about 40% of its area) and once housed Macau's first roller coaster, inside an artificial volcano topped by a Potala Palace replica.
deep_cut_fact: Besides his gaming and tourism businesses, he has served as Honorary Consul of the Republic of Cape Verde to the Macau SAR.
notes: Full name Chow Kam Fai, David (周錦輝). Fortune largely eroded: GGRAsia reported in April 2025 he held only ~0.39% of Macau Legend after a debt settlement. Forbes listing is from 2014 only. No personal published contact found; outreach would have to go via Macau business channels.

name: Gregory Bentley
current_role: Executive Chair, Bentley Systems (Nasdaq: BSY), Exton, Pennsylvania
profile: Greg Bentley joined Bentley Systems - the infrastructure-engineering software company (MicroStation, digital twins) founded by his brothers Barry and Keith in 1984 - in 1991 and was CEO from 2000 until July 2024, when Nicholas Cumins became the first non-family CEO. He now serves as executive chair; the family retains majority control of the ~$1.2-1.5bn-revenue company.
interesting_fact: After the Space Shuttle Challenger disaster in 1986, NASA used Bentley Systems software to build 3D models of the launch to help analyse what went wrong. Before their software ventures, the Bentley brothers sold Christmas trees for extra cash.
deep_cut_fact: Before Bentley, he founded a financial trading software firm that became part of SunGard Data Systems, and he sat on SunGard's S&P 500 board from 1991 to 2005. He is a Drexel University trustee and chairs the advisory board of its Pennoni Honors College. He calls Bentley's customers 'users', not customers, because of the ongoing relationship.
notes: Strong fit for a data-center/infrastructure podcast (digital twins of energy and infrastructure assets). The IR email is also the published route for contacting the board (investors.bentley.com/contact-the-board).

name: Ling Shisheng
current_role: Chairman and General Manager, Hangzhou AllTest Biotech (杭州安旭生物科技股份有限公司, 'Assure Tech', SSE STAR: 688075)
profile: Ling Shisheng (凌世生, b. 1972), a Zhejiang University genetics graduate, founded Hangzhou-based point-of-care (POCT) rapid-diagnostics maker Assure Tech in 2008-09 with his wife and vice-chair Jiang Xueying. COVID-19 antigen test demand (over 90% of sales overseas) drove a STAR Market IPO in November 2021 and put the couple on the Hurun list in 2022.
interesting_fact: Before running her husband's company, co-owner and vice-chair Jiang Xueying spent nearly two decades as a court judge in Shengzhou and Hangzhou's Xihu District.
deep_cut_fact: A trained geneticist (MSc, Zhejiang University; senior engineer), he started as a researcher at Hangzhou University's School of Life Sciences (1996-97), then spent ten years as R&D director at ACON Biotech (Hangzhou) before founding his own diagnostics firm.
notes: Emails are those of the board secretary (Han Jun) and securities affairs representative (Yu Jun) as published in the 2025 annual report summary. Low English-language profile; outreach probably needs to be in Chinese. Wealth tied to pandemic-era testing boom.

name: Deng Ke
current_role: Director and General Manager (CEO), YD Electronic Technology Co., Ltd. (奕东电子, SZSE: 301123), Dongguan
profile: Deng Ke (邓可, b. 1985) runs YD Electronic Technology, the Dongguan precision-components maker (FPC, connector components, LED backlight modules) founded in 1997 by his father, chairman Deng Yuquan. He has led the company as general manager since its 2019 restructuring ahead of its 2021 Shenzhen ChiNext listing; the family fortune is shared with his father.
interesting_fact: YD worked with Amphenol in 2007 to develop Amphenol's first SFP (optical-transceiver) component, taking it into high-speed connectors for data and telecom equipment; in 2013 it co-developed what it calls the industry's first FPC for EV battery management systems.
deep_cut_fact: He earned a master's at Imperial College London and, from 2009 (aged about 24), headed YD's then-new FPC (flexible printed circuit) business group - now one of its core businesses - before becoming general manager.
notes: 'YDET' in the source data = YD Electronic Technology (ydet.com). Father Deng Yuquan (b. 1959) is chairman and a former engineer at state-owned Factory 733. Optical-communications components link to the data-center theme. Low English-language media profile.

name: Johnathan Oringer
current_role: Founder, Chief Executive Officer and Chairman, Shutterstock (NYSE: SSTK) - back as CEO since October 2026
profile: Programmer-photographer Jon Oringer founded Shutterstock in 2003 with his own savings and about 30,000 of his own photos, built it into a global stock-media marketplace and took it public in 2012, becoming known as New York's first tech billionaire. He was executive chairman from 2020; after the planned Getty Images merger was terminated in July 2026, he returned as CEO in October 2026.
interesting_fact: To seed Shutterstock he bought a Canon Rebel and shot about 100,000 photos himself in six months, launching with a culled set of 30,000 images, a 600 sq ft office and a $49/month unlimited-download subscription.
deep_cut_fact: As a Stony Brook student in the 1990s he wrote and sold thousands of copies of one of the web's first pop-up blockers and ran about ten one-person subscription software startups (personal firewalls, cookie blockers, trademark managers); he is also a certified commercial helicopter pilot.
notes: Very current: per the Nov 2026 proxy (DEF 14A) he became CEO and Chairman in October 2026 after the Getty Images merger agreement was terminated on July 7, 2026. Shutterstock's AI data-licensing business (selling training data to AI labs) is a natural podcast angle.

name: Cesar Mata Pires
current_role: Deceased (founder and largest shareholder of Brazilian construction group OAS)
profile: César de Araújo Mata Pires (born Salvador, Bahia, 19 Jan 1950), civil engineer and founder of the construction group OAS, died in São Paulo on 22 August 2017, aged 67.
notes: Died 22 August 2017 (Portuguese Wikipedia). Not a candidate for outreach.

name: Suzan Sabanci Dincer
current_role: Chairperson, Akbank; board member, Sabancı Holding
profile: Third-generation member of Turkey's Sabancı family (b. 1965; now goes by Suzan Sabancı), a treasury and risk-management banker who joined Akbank in 1989 as EVP for treasury and has chaired the bank since March 2008. She also sits on the boards of Sabancı Holding, the Institute of International Finance, and Blackstone's international advisory board.
interesting_fact: Queen Elizabeth II appointed her a CBE in 2012 for developing Turkey-UK relations (she chaired the Turkish-British Business Council 2010-14), and King Felipe VI awarded her Spain's Order of Civil Merit in 2014.
deep_cut_fact: She served as Honorary Consul of Luxembourg in Istanbul for 17 years (2005-2022), and is a founding member and board member of Endeavor Turkey, the high-impact entrepreneurship network - a natural hook for an entrepreneurship podcast.
notes: Now uses the name Suzan Sabancı (dropped 'Dinçer'). Akbank IR page also lists individual IR team emails; no personal channel published. Endeavor Turkey is a possible warm route.
